newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bank insurance law boosts bank capitalization.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bank insurance law boosts bank capitalization.

text.p: The 1991 overhaul of U.S. federal bank deposit insurance laws has helped the banking industry reach its best ever level of capitalization, U.S. Comptroller of the Currency Eugene Ludwig.
"The banking industry is better capitalized than at any time in our professional lifetime," Ludwig said in a speech to the Brookings Institute think-tank.
Ludwig said the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation Improvement Act of 1991 was in part responsible for banks' improved capitalization.

"There should be little doubt that FDICIA is part of the reason for the positive capital picture we see today," he said. The new law "has advanced the banking industry's safety and soundness, focused by encouraging banks' management to better identify and control risk."

But Ludwig cautioned that the long-term impact of the 1991 law was still unknown. "I have to say that five years is too short a time to be certain of its true impact -- particularly when those five years have been characterised by continued strengthening in the general economy," Ludwig said.
